_description: Task13 DRIFT field, COARSE transcription -- the 0.22mm far-field grid for the 5x5 LArPix v2a tile at the true 4.4mm pitch. The fine sibling (example_gen_pcb_drift_pixel_task13_fine.json) carries the true design values unsnapped. SNAPPED PAD/GAP, AND WHY ONLY HERE: the design values are pixelSize 3.5, pixelGap 0.9, chamfer_r 0.7. gcd(35,9) = 1, so NO spacing coarser than 0.1mm divides both the pad and the gap exactly and some snapping on the coarse grid is unavoidable. 0.22mm was chosen because it snaps the pad to 3.52mm, only +1.1% in area, against +5.8% for 0.2 or 0.4. That error matters more than it looks: the far field in the final stitched output IS the upsampled coarse solution, so a coarse pad-area error biases the far weighting field by about the same percentage, and it is a SMOOTH error that the Laplacian residual metric cannot detect. The design values are preserved as the _design_* keys below; the generators ignore _design_* keys. CELL COUNTS AT 0.22mm: pixelSize 3.52 -> 16 cells, pixelGap 0.88 -> 4 cells, chamfer_r 0.66 -> 3 cells (0.7/0.22 = 3.18). PITCH MUST STAY EXACTLY 4.4mm = 20 coarse cells: 16 + 4 = 20. hybrid_iterate.py _cells() requires the transverse extent to be a WHOLE number of cells and raises otherwise, so this is a hard constraint, not a preference; if pixelSize and pixelGap do not sum to 4.4 the periodic drift tile is wrong. DEPTH: driftZDepth 79.15 is the electron launch node and is deliberately NOT rounded to 79.2. The key is overloaded -- it sets both the grounded cathode node and the path start z in continuous mm. hybrid_iterate._extents puts the cathode at ceil((driftZDepth + MIN_CATHODE_CLEARANCE)/coarse) = ceil(79.15/0.22) = 360 coarse cells = 79.2mm, the last plane of the 361-node coarse z grid, so there is NO dead space above the cathode; but the launch z 79.15 does not land on that node, which is what we want. Snapping driftZDepth would put the drift start exactly on the grounded Dirichlet node. The weighting generator's own cathode grounding uses int(round(driftZDepth/spacing)) = 360, i.e. the same plane. CATHODE FORMULA, so the value can be recomputed by hand when the drift length or the bulk field changes: CathodePotential = -BulkField * (driftZDepth - pixelPlaneLowEdgePosition). The value is maintained BY HAND on purpose, so the bulk field stays a visible, editable number rather than a derived one. NOTE: CathodePotential -8400 was NOT re-derived when this file was retargeted from the 159.9mm depth. The drift length is now 79.15 - 10.0 = 69.15mm, so -8400 V is 121.5 V/mm nominal, not the 56.04 V/mm the old 149.9mm geometry gave. Re-derive it before running. TILE SIZE: Npixels 5, i.e. a 5x5 pad tile at the 4.4mm pitch = 22.0mm transverse for the weighting probe; the DRIFT field is one periodic tile, so Npixels does not size this file's domain. GridPotential does NOT enter the cathode calculation: the shield grid has holes and is transparent at the tile centre, so it is not an equipotential plane terminating the field. The bulk field is set by the CATHODE against the PIXEL PLANE at 0 V. GridPotential instead sets the collection field between the grid and the pads.
